items.prompt: Order the phases for one right-boundary step of a longest-valid variable window.
constraints: Expansion may make the window invalid.
The answer is maximum valid length.

elements.text: Add the right-boundary element to maintained state.
While invalid, remove left-boundary state and advance left.
Update the maximum with the restored valid length.

feedback.reason: Expansion changes state first, invalidity is then repaired, and only the resulting legal range may update a longest-valid answer.

blocks.text: The phases correspond to three different states: the old valid range, the post-expansion range that may be invalid, and the repaired legal range. A repair phase may perform zero removals when expansion preserves validity.

items: Add the element at `right` so maintained state describes the newly expanded range.
While that state violates the constraint, remove the contribution at `left` and advance `left`.
Once legal, compare `right-left+1` with the longest answer.

blocks.title: Only legal ranges update a longest-valid answer
blocks.text: Updating before repair scores an invalid range; repairing before adding tests the old range. The same dependency applies to sum, frequency, and budget predicates when their removal rule is legal.

items.prompt: Order the operations for processing a new right-boundary value when minimizing the length of a positive-value window with sum at least a positive target T.
constraints: The current sum after expansion is at least T.
T is positive.
Only nonempty ranges are answer candidates.
The inner steps repeat while the window remains valid.

elements.text: Add the incoming right-boundary value.
Record the current valid length as a minimum candidate.
Subtract the value at the current left boundary.
Advance the left boundary, then repeat the valid-loop test.

feedback.reason: A shortest candidate must be recorded while it is still valid, before the outgoing value is removed and left advances.

blocks.text: Expansion may establish `sum >= T`. The remaining three operations form the body of a while-valid loop: record before mutating the witnessed candidate, then keep state and boundary movement synchronized.

items: Add the incoming value so the sum describes the range ending at the new `right`.
While `sum >= T`, record the current nonempty length as a minimum candidate.
Subtract `a[left]` while `left` still identifies the outgoing value.
Advance `left`, then test `sum >= T` again to discover a shorter valid suffix.

blocks.title: Record before removal
blocks.text: Removing first can erase the last valid candidate. Advancing `left` before subtraction targets the wrong value unless the outgoing value was cached.

items.prompt: Order the transition from building the first fixed-size window to evaluating the second one.
constraints: k is a positive integer.
The input contains at least k+1 values, so both the first and second windows exist.
The first k−1 values are already in state before these operations begin.

elements.text: Add the kth value to complete the first legal window.
Evaluate the first length-k window.
Add the next right-boundary value, temporarily creating k+1 elements.
Remove the original leftmost value and advance left.
Evaluate the restored second length-k window.

feedback.reason: Initialization produces a legal size-k state before any removal; later expansions require one outgoing removal before evaluation.

blocks.text: Initialization and steady-state sliding have different preconditions. The first window has no outgoing predecessor; the second does.

items: Add the kth value to the existing k-1 values, completing the first legal length-k window.
Add the next value, temporarily producing k+1 represented elements.
Remove the original leftmost contribution and advance `left`, restoring length k.

blocks.title: Initialization has no outgoing value
blocks.text: Applying steady-state removal while building the first window keeps it below k. Omitting removal after the next expansion evaluates k+1 elements.

items.prompt: A running-sum window uses `left += 1; sum -= a[left]` when removing the outgoing element. What is the precise defect?
constraints: Before the two statements, left points to the element that must leave.
No outgoing value was cached separately.

options.text: The same outgoing element is subtracted twice.
The two orders are equivalent because addition and subtraction commute.
Advancing first changes which element a[left] names, so the code subtracts the new leftmost value instead of the outgoing one.
Incrementing left also increments right implicitly.

feedback.reason: Boundary mutation changes the identity referenced by `a[left]`; remove state for the old boundary before advancing it.

blocks.text: The outgoing element is defined by the pre-move left boundary. If left is incremented first and the value was not cached, `a[left]` refers to the element that should remain in the window. The aggregate then contains the old outgoing value and lacks the new leftmost value, so state and boundaries diverge. Arithmetic commutativity does not help because the operands differ. Caching `outgoing = a[left]` before increment can make another concrete order safe, but the semantic dependency remains: identify/remove the old element before losing its boundary reference.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.subtracts_twice: Only one subtraction occurs; the issue is that it targets the wrong array element.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.right_boundary_changes: The right index is independent; the defect is stale state relative to the left boundary.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.only_style: The operations use different values after the index changes, so they are not algebraically interchangeable.

items.prompt: Order the phases for a longest window with a frequency cap after a new right-boundary value arrives.
constraints: The new value itself may create the violation.
The answer is updated only for a legal window.

elements.text: Increment the incoming value's frequency in the maintained state.
Evaluate the validity predicate on the post-expansion state.
While invalid, decrement outgoing frequencies, remove zero-count keys as needed, and advance left.
Update the longest answer from the repaired window.

feedback.reason: The violation is defined by the state after the incoming frequency changes; repair and answer evaluation follow that state transition.

blocks.text: The frequency predicate is meaningful only after state includes the incoming occurrence. The repair phase is conditional and may perform zero removals, but it always precedes answer evaluation.

items: Increment the incoming key's frequency so state represents the expanded range.
Evaluate the cap or distinct-count predicate on that post-expansion state.
While invalid, decrement outgoing frequencies, delete zero-count keys when required, and advance `left`.
Update the longest answer from the resulting legal range.

blocks.title: Do not validate the old range
blocks.text: Checking before incrementing certifies only the previous window and cannot see a new over-cap occurrence or a (K+1)th distinct key.

items.prompt: A repaired at-most-K window must count every valid contiguous range ending at the current right boundary. Order the phases for one right-boundary step.
constraints: After repair, every start from left through right forms a valid suffix.
The answer counts ranges rather than finding their maximum length.
The incoming value may make the pre-repair window invalid.

elements.text: Add the incoming value to the maintained state.
Remove from the left while the constraint is violated.
Add right − left + 1 to the total count.

feedback.reason: The suffix count is valid only after the current right boundary has been added and the left boundary has restored the constraint.

blocks.text: Before expansion, the state describes the previous endpoint. After expansion it may contain too many distinct values or another violation. Once repair finishes, each start in [left, right] produces a valid suffix ending at right, so the contribution is right−left+1. Counting before repair includes invalid starts; counting only one range loses the other valid suffixes.

items.prompt: A fixed-size window reports its maximum with a decreasing deque of indices. Order the update steps after a new value arrives at index right.
constraints: Deque indices increase from front to back.
Deque values decrease from front to back.
Only indices inside the current length-k window may remain.

elements.text: Remove deque-front indices that are left of the new window.
Remove back indices whose values are no greater than the incoming value.
Append right to the deque.
Use the deque front as the maximum for the complete window.

feedback.reason: Expiration enforces window membership, dominance enforces value order, append adds the new candidate, and only then can the front represent the current maximum.

blocks.text: The deque stores indices rather than only values so expiration can be checked against the left boundary. An expired front cannot contribute. A smaller value behind the incoming value can never become the maximum before the incoming value leaves, so it is removed from the back. The incoming index is then appended, and the front is the maximum once the current window has reached length k.

items.prompt: A longest-valid window receives a new value and remains valid, so the repair loop removes nothing. What is the correct next action?
constraints: The answer is maximum valid length.
The maintained state already includes the incoming value.
The validity loop has been checked and performs zero iterations.

options.text: Update the longest answer from right − left + 1; a zero-iteration repair still leaves a legal window.
Skip answer evaluation because a window is useful only after at least one left-boundary removal.
Remove one leftmost value to force progress before evaluating.
Evaluate the old answer before the incoming value is included in state.

feedback.reason: The repair phase is conditional; its purpose is to restore legality, not to force a boundary movement on every iteration.

blocks.text: After the incoming value is added, the current range may already satisfy the constraint. In that case left remains the correct earliest start, and the full range ending at right is a legal candidate. Updating after a zero-iteration while loop is essential for monotone longest-window scans. Removing an arbitrary value would discard a valid prefix and could shorten the answer.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.skip_until_shrink: A valid window does not need a repair event before it can improve the maximum.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.shrink_one_anyway: Forced removal discards a legal start without a violation-based reason.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.evaluate_before_add: The answer must include the new right-boundary value and use post-expansion state.

items.prompt: A fixed-size window counts records satisfying predicate P. After the first complete window, order the state operations for each new incoming record.
constraints: The count must describe exactly k records.
The maintained count stores the number of records satisfying P.
The outgoing record is still addressed by left at the start.

elements.text: Add the incoming record's contribution to the count.
Subtract the outgoing record's contribution.
Advance left beyond the removed record.
Emit or evaluate the count for the restored length-k window.

feedback.reason: The count is a one-in/one-out aggregate, and the answer is evaluated only after state and boundaries again describe k records.

blocks.text: The incoming record contributes before the outgoing record is removed, creating a temporary k+1 state. Subtracting the outgoing predicate result while left still names it keeps the count addressable. Advancing left then restores the exact-length window, which is the first state eligible for output.

items.prompt: A positive-value shortest-threshold window is valid before removing its leftmost value, but becomes invalid immediately after that removal. When is the last candidate recorded?
constraints: The objective is minimum nonempty length with sum at least T.
The window is valid before the removal.
The outgoing removal makes the sum fall below T.

options.text: Record the current valid length before subtracting the outgoing value; the post-removal window is not a candidate.
Record the shorter post-removal length because it is closer to the optimum even though its sum is below T.
Record only the window that existed before the current right value was added.
Discard the current candidate because the shrink loop ended without another valid window.

feedback.reason: The shortest valid candidate is witnessed immediately before the removal that breaks the threshold.

blocks.text: The shrinking loop records each valid window before it mutates the left boundary. The final valid state may be followed by an invalid state, but that does not erase the candidate already recorded. The post-removal range violates sum >= T and cannot enter the answer merely because it is shorter. This is why shortest-window answer updates occur before outgoing-state mutation.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.record_after_invalid: Length alone is insufficient; the candidate must still satisfy the threshold.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.record_before_expand_only: The current right-boundary value may create the shortest valid candidate and must be included.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.discard_last_candidate: The last valid state remains a legal answer even when the next shrink makes the state invalid.

items.prompt: In a positive-sum threshold window, when should the newly expanded right value enter the running sum?
constraints: The stated window contract applies.
The input boundary cases remain legal.

options.text: Add it before checking whether the window reaches the threshold.
Check the old sum first.
Shrink before adding the new value.
Reset the sum whenever right advances.

feedback.reason: The accepted option preserves the window invariant and output semantics.

blocks.text: The boundary update order and stored aggregate must represent exactly the current contiguous window. Pointer movement is correct only when this invariant remains true.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.check_before_add: That misses a window ending at right.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.add_after_shrink: The new value is part of the candidate.

items.prompt: For a shortest-valid-window objective, what order is correct after the sum becomes valid?
constraints: The stated window contract applies.
The input boundary cases remain legal.

options.text: Record the valid length, then remove left values while validity remains true and record each new valid length.
Shrink without recording until invalid.
Remove once and record even if invalid.
Expand before considering removal.

feedback.reason: The accepted option preserves the window invariant and output semantics.

blocks.text: The boundary update order and stored aggregate must represent exactly the current contiguous window. Pointer movement is correct only when this invariant remains true.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.shrink_only: The last valid state is missed.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.expand: That moves away from a shortest candidate.

items.prompt: What should a variable-window repair loop guarantee?
constraints: The stated window contract applies.
The input boundary cases remain legal.

options.text: Every repair advances left and updates outgoing state, so left never moves backward.
Reset left to zero after every violation.
Keep left fixed and move right until validity returns.
Move either boundary arbitrarily.

feedback.reason: The accepted option preserves the window invariant and output semantics.

blocks.text: The boundary update order and stored aggregate must represent exactly the current contiguous window. Pointer movement is correct only when this invariant remains true.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.right_only: For positive sums, expansion cannot repair an oversized window.

constraints: The stated window contract applies.
The input boundary cases remain legal.

options.text: Leave the window empty, keep its sum identity, and continue expanding right.
Record length -1 as the best window.
Reset right to zero and restart.
Add a zero value to restore the threshold.

feedback.reason: The accepted option preserves the window invariant and output semantics.
